tldr: This thread groups independent arXiv papers on one theme, not one event: agents improving their own skills while the model stays fixed. A coding-agent paper (Oct 26) added hierarchical skills, ScienceCUA (Nov 2) built skills from software manuals, and EvoGuard (Nov 4) targeted degradation when skills evolve online.
whats_new: Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution (Nov 10) is the fourth skill-evolution paper in the thread, pitching skills that are patched with program support, with model parameters left untouched.
why_it_matters: Skills are editable artifacts, so agent behavior can change without retraining; online evolution can also make skills worse, so every accepted edit needs a guard.

beats.headline: Hierarchical skills separate reusable experience from repo-specific context
ScienceCUA builds skills from manuals and evolves them by execution
EvoGuard targets degradation in online skill evolution
beats.summary: The first paper in the thread to treat skill evolution itself as a failure source.

beats.headline: A program-aided approach makes skill evolution patchable

open_questions: Do evolved skills hold up on tasks and repositories outside their training benchmark?
Does skill evolution beat hand-written skills on a shared benchmark?
Does EvoGuard's mitigation hold when applied to other skill evolvers?
Do patch-level skill edits degrade less under online evolution than whole-document rewrites?
take_for_builders: Version agent skills like code: keep each evolved edit as a reviewable diff, gate it on a grader or benchmark, and keep a rollback path in case online evolution degrades performance.
